title: Banjoist Willie Santiago and the fish in the sun
summary: A story of Willie Santiago, who slept through jobs, and the night he was to cook for the club, bought a red snapper, got drunk and fell asleep under a tree with the fish in the sun.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well, I've got to tell you this little story about

this Willie Santiago. He was the banjo player in New Orleans. You know, he used to come in at night and he'd sleep. He'd tune up his banjo and he'd go to sleep all night. Time to knock off or get off -- it was about ten to 15 minutes before we would knock off, he'd stretch himself and say, "Oh, boy, I feel good." And everybody in the band would say, "You should feel good. You slept all night."

And we'd go out and they had a club and everybody's turn -- whoever's turn it was -- they had to fill, they had what they call in those days a "cooler." They put ice in there and they'd fill it with wine and they had to cook the dinner for the club. And it was Willie's turn that night, that day, in fact, it was a Friday. So he went out and he bought a big fish, a big red snapper, filled the cooler full of wine, and he went out and got the fish when the market opened early in the morning, six o'clock. And he got stoned and he slept under a tree on [Claiborne] Avenue, it was the trees, and he went to sleep under the tree and the sun hit him and the fish. And they were talking about the flies, and everybody was just around looking at him and just laughing. And, boy, did they kid him about that. Oh, God, it was -- we used to have a lot of fun.
